corrections.claim: The spec's code_locations enumerate every surviving cross-reference to fig 2 / fig 17 (reader's guide L55, hero md L186-187/190/192, hero comments L206-208/220/246-247/280-281, fig01 md L368, fig01 fig.text L476-480).
corrections.correct_fact: IT MISSES builder line 4357, inside the §5b 'Scope of validity' markdown (cell 47, which SURVIVES the deletion): 'The measured mean $y\simeq1.0\times10^{-6}$ and mean $\tau\simeq1.8\times10^{-3}$ (printed live by the fig-2 cell)'. This is both a dangling cross-reference and a hard provenance break. `grep -n 'mean tau'` returns exactly one hit — line 603, fig02's print — and the executed cell-8 stream confirms it: 'kappa rms = 0.0225; mean tau = 1.803e-03; mean y = 1.045e-06'. The hero's print (lines 321-327, cell-4 stream) emits mean y (1.045e-06, survives) but NO mean tau. Deleting fig02's code cell therefore leaves a surviving markdown cell quoting a number that no cell in the notebook computes — a direct violation of the notebook's own stated rule at lines 60-61 ('every quantitative statement is printed by a code cell in this notebook or traceable to a named cache; nothing is quoted from memory'). Required additional step: either add `mean tau = {tau_fid0.mean():.3e}` to the hero print at line 323-327 and re-point line 4357 at the hero cell, or keep fig02's print.

corrections.claim: Risk 'MEMORY UPSIDE': removing ~8.6 GB of sequential npz I/O 'materially eases the ~10 GB cgroup'.
corrections.correct_fact: The notebook is not executed in the ~10 GB session cgroup. run_figures.sbatch requests `#SBATCH --mem=128G` (plus 16 CPUs and one A100) and runs `_build_figures_nb.py` then `_run_figures_nb.py` there. The ~10 GB/1-CPU cgroup is this interactive agent session's limit only. The I/O-volume arithmetic (3 + 6 = 9 loads × ~0.95 GB ≈ 8.6 GB) is correct, and the loads are sequential with del/gc so peak RSS was never near 8.6 GB anyway — the memory framing is a non-argument for the deletion.

corrections.claim: data_verified: 'Only differences: (i) hero's kappa Normalize uses 2*std of the DMO map (±0.0374) vs fig02's ±0.0367; (ii) fig02 draws theta_x/theta_y degree axes+ticks, hero replaces them with a single 1-degree scale bar.' (i.e. fig02 panels a,b,c are a strict subset of hero panels b,c,d)
corrections.correct_fact: Two further real differences the spec omits. (iii) PANEL SIZE: fig02 is `plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(TWO_COL[0], 2.7))` with TWO_COL=(7.2, 3.1) (paper_style.py:28) → ~2.2 in per panel; the hero's top row is 4 panels in a 2×4 gridspec of a (7.2, 5.0) figure with height_ratios=[1.0, 2.05] → ~1.6 in wide and ~1.4 in tall per panel. The map suite renders the same maps ~40% larger linearly, with quantitative degree axes. (iv) PRINTED NUMBERS: fig02's print (line 603) reports the UNSMOOTHED painted kappa rms (0.0225) and mean tau (1.803e-03); the hero prints neither (its 0.0183 is the SMOOTHED painted kappa rms). So the two cells' printed provenance is not a subset relation either — see the line-4357 correction.

additional_findings: OPERATIONAL GOTCHA THE SPEC OMITS — the EDITS_READY gate is already open. run_figures.sbatch waits up to 4 h for a sentinel file `EDITS_READY` in papers/01_pipeline/ and bails with RUN_FAILED if it never appears. That file ALREADY EXISTS (98 B, Jul 28 16:06), as does RUN_DONE (8 B, Jul 28 16:26). So the gate provides zero protection: a job submitted while the builder is half-edited will proceed immediately to `python _build_figures_nb.py` + `python _run_figures_nb.py`. Whoever executes CR-3 should `rm EDITS_READY` before starting the edits and re-create it when the builder is final and syntax-checked, matching the sbatch's documented intent.

EVIDENCE THAT PARTIAL RE-EXECUTION IS THE ESTABLISHED PRACTICE (contra step 12's 'a full re-execute becomes necessary in practice'). Only figs_v2/fig00_hero.pdf (Jul 29 12:19) and fig02_map_suite.pdf (Jul 29 12:20) postdate the Jul 28 17:2x batch; the notebook's execution_counts are non-monotonic — [(2,1),(4,2),(6,3),(8,3),(10,5),(13,6),…] — i.e. cells 4 and 8 were re-run interactively after Slurm job 2454501. Step 12's point still stands for a REBUILD (build() discards all outputs), but the executor should know a targeted Jupyter re-run of the single fig01 cell is what has actually been done before, and requires only small inputs (stage1_slab00.npz + three composite_slab00.npz + the design array) — no ~1 GB map loads.
